I've written the contract into `src/utils.ts`. Both checks pass: `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors, and `vitest run` passes all 442 tests in 13 files. Only `src/utils.ts` changed.

- **`joinURL`** already existed, but the spec gives it a new signature, `(base: string, ...input: string[])`. Since the existing body has to stay as it is, I added that signature as an overload just above the current implementation, which I left alone. Callers see the spec's signature; the current relative-aware logic still runs, so the existing tests and `withBase` behave as before until the implementer rewrites it. I also updated its doc comment to describe the new plain join.
- **`joinRelativeURL(..._input: string[]): string`** is new. Its body is the `not implemented` stub, and its doc comment uses the spec's wording and one of its examples (`"/a", "../b", "./c"` → `"/b/c"`).

The spec says neither function throws, so I added no error types or constants.

Because of the overload, calls with no arguments (`joinURL()`) or with a spread of a plain `string[]` (as the existing `test/join.test.ts` does) are type errors. That doesn't stop the tests from running: the type check only covers `src`, and vitest doesn't type-check.

Exported names added: `joinRelativeURL` (plus the new `joinURL(base: string, ...input: string[])` overload signature)

I wrote the public suite in `test/ufo-join-relative.test.ts`. It has one flat test per example row in the spec, and every scenario is covered. Each test name starts with its scenario key and shows the call and the expected result, for example `[boundary-7] joinRelativeURL("/a", "../../../d") === "../d"`.

**How the keys map to the spec:**
- **`joinURL`:** `[happy-1..3]`, `[boundary-1..5]`, `[unhappy-1]`
- **`joinRelativeURL`:** `[happy-4..6]`, `[boundary-6..13]`, `[unhappy-2]`
- **`withBase`:** `[happy-7]`, `[boundary-14]`

**Choices you might trip over:**
- **Every row, not one per scenario:** you asked for a happy path and one boundary case per scenario. I wrote a test for every example row instead, since the spec states each one exactly. As in `test/join.test.ts`, the rows sit in tables and a small helper loops over them, so all tests stay at the top level with unique names.
- **Calls the types reject:** a few rows call with no arguments, `undefined` or `null`, which the signatures don't allow. Those calls are cast so they still type-check. No other non-string values are tested.

**Results:**
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors.
- `npx vitest run test/ufo-join-relative.`: 86 tests fail and 38 pass.
  - Every `joinRelativeURL` test fails because the body throws `not implemented`.
  - `joinURL` was not stubbed. It still has the old relative-aware body, so its rows where old and new behaviour match already pass.
  - The `joinURL` and `withBase` rows that fail are those where the spec changes the result, such as `"/a", "../b"` now giving `"/a/../b"`.

124 tests, in 1 file.

I wrote 136 hidden tests in two files under `test/hidden-ufo-join-relative/`. All 136 fail against the code as it stands, and `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors.

I checked the expected values by implementing the spec in a scratch copy of the repo, outside this folder. All 136 hidden tests pass there. So do 123 of the 124 public tests; the one that fails is the contradiction listed at the end.

- **`join-url.test.ts` (55 tests):**
  - `joinURL`: happy-1 to 3, boundary-1 to 4 and unhappy-1.
  - `withBase`: happy-7 and boundary-14.
- **`join-relative-url.test.ts` (81 tests):** `joinRelativeURL`, covering happy-4 to 6, boundary-6 to 13 and unhappy-2.

The tests target the shortcuts most likely to pass the public suite:
- **`joinURL`:**
  - stripping every leading slash (`"a", "///b"` must give `"a///b"`);
  - parsing out the query or fragment (`"http://x.com/p?q=1", "r"` must give `"http://x.com/p?q=1/r"`);
  - keeping the trailing slash from a final `"/"` input (`"a", "b", "/"` must give `"a/b"`);
  - treating a falsy base as a separate step (`undefined, "/", "a"` must give `"a"`).
- **`joinRelativeURL`:**
  - POSIX-style resolution, which keeps every unmatched `..` (`"../../a"` must give `"../a"`);
  - treating `scheme://` specially;
  - choosing the first and last input before dropping falsy ones.
- **`withBase`:** switching it to `joinRelativeURL`.

**Gaps:**
- **boundary-5 (base `"/"` with nothing after it) has no hidden test.** The current `joinURL` body is still the old algorithm, not a `not implemented` stub, and it already returns `"/"` for every input of this kind. Any test of it would pass today, which breaks the rule that every test must fail now. The public tests cover it.
- **Some happy-7 and `joinURL` cases go unused for the same reason.** Where the old and new `joinURL` agree, a test would pass today. So the hidden happy-7 tests use a base with a protocol (`withBase("/bar", "http://x.com")` must give `"http://x.com/bar"`), and every hidden `joinURL` case gives a different result under the old algorithm.

136 tests, in 2 files.

Open in the spec:
- `[happy-7] withBase("/", "/foo/") === "/foo/"`: the spec contradicts itself here. Its `withBase` rule returns `joinURL(withoutTrailingSlash(base), input)`, which is `joinURL("/foo", "/")`. The `joinURL` rule skips a `"/"` input after the base, which gives `"/foo"` (boundary-4 has `"/a", "/"` giving `"/a"`). The example table says `"/foo/"` instead. The spec doesn't settle which result is right, so neither suite should test it until that's decided.

The `joinURL` rule skips a `"/"` input after the base, which gives `"/foo"` (boundary-4 has `"/a", "/"` giving `"/a"`). The example table says `"/foo/"` instead. The spec doesn't settle which result is right, so neither suite should test it until that's decided.
